title: Geometric restriction between topoi of internal group actions
statement:
Fix a universe and a small site $(C,J)$ with finite limits [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Put $\mathscr E=\operatorname{Sh}(C,J)$, and let $K,L$ be sheaves of groups with values in that universe. A $K$-object is a sheaf of sets $X$ together with a sheaf morphism $K\times X\to X$ satisfying the identity and associativity equations; morphisms are equivariant sheaf maps. Write $\mathscr E^K$ for this category. For the action site $C_K$ with arrows $(f,a):V\to U$, $a\in K(V)$, composition $(f,a)(g,b)=(fg,bg^*a)$ and topology generated by covers whose underlying base families cover [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation], there is an equivalence $\mathscr E^K\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(C_K)$. It sends an action to the presheaf with restriction $x\mapsto a\cdot f^*x$. In particular $\mathscr E^K$ is a topos presented by a small site.

For every morphism of group sheaves $\theta:L\to K$, restriction of action $q_\theta^{-1}:\mathscr E^K\to\mathscr E^L$ has a right adjoint and preserves finite limits, so is the inverse image of a geometric morphism $q_\theta:\mathscr E^L\to\mathscr E^K$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. There is a geometric morphism $p_K:\mathscr E^K\to\mathscr E$ whose inverse image equips a sheaf with trivial action. The equality $q_\theta^{-1}p_K^{-1}=p_L^{-1}$ on sheaves and maps specifies a canonical geometric isomorphism $p_Kq_\theta\cong p_L$. Identity and successive restrictions carry their literal identity and composition identifications.

Let $R$ be any sheaf of commutative rings on $C$ and put $R_K=p_K^{-1}R$, $R_L=p_L^{-1}R$. On the ringed topoi $(\mathscr E^K,R_K)$ and $(\mathscr E^L,R_L)$, the module pullbacks along $p_K$ and $q_\theta$ are respectively trivial inflation and restriction of action, and are exact. Under the action-site equivalence their tensor comparisons send $x\otimes y$ to $x\otimes y$ with the diagonal action and their unit comparisons are the identity on the regular ring. A ring-sheaf map $\varphi:R\to R'$ induces the same map on these trivially acted-on ring sheaves. The resulting squares with $p_K$ and $q_\theta$ commute as ringed-topos morphisms, with identity comparison on underlying sheaves.

proof.text: Use the small category and topology of [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation]. At the presheaf level define $E(X)(U)=X(U)$ and $E(X)(f,a)(x)=a\cdot f^*x$. The calculation $b\cdot g^*(a\cdot f^*x)=(b\,g^*a)\cdot(fg)^*x$ proves functoriality with precisely the stated order of multiplication. Conversely, for a presheaf $N$ on $C_K$, put $X(f)=N(f,1)$ and $a\cdot x=N(1_U,a)(x)$. Since $(1,b)\circ(1,a)=(1,ab)$, contravariance gives the left-action law. The equality $(1_U,a)\circ(f,1)=(f,f^*a)=(f,1)\circ(1_V,f^*a)$ gives naturality of the action. Finally $(f,a)=(f,1)\circ(1_V,a)$ recovers every map of $N$. A natural transformation for all $(f,a)$ is exactly a map natural for $(f,1)$ and equivariant for $(1,a)$. These constructions are inverse on objects and morphisms.

Check the sheaf condition, rather than inferring the set-valued assertion from a module equivalence. By [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation], a sieve $S$ on $U$ covers precisely when $S_1=\{f\mid(f,1)\in S\}$ is a covering base sieve. The matching-family definition is [def-weil-pbc-topos]. The base sieves needed here are those of the topology generated by the covering families of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]: by its axioms (i)–(iii) (isomorphisms, composition, base change), the sieves containing the sieve $\langle U_i\to U\rangle$ generated by some covering family satisfy (i)–(iii) of [def-weil-pbc-topos], and every topology in which these generated sieves cover contains them, so they are exactly the generated covering sieves. A sheaf $X$ for covering families glues on such a sieve $T\supseteq\langle u_i:U_i\to U\rangle$: a matching family $(x_f)_{f\in T}$ gives sections $x_{u_i}$ agreeing on $U_i\times_UU_j$, hence a unique $x$ with $x|_{U_i}=x_{u_i}$; for $f:V\to U$ in $T$, $x|_V$ and $x_f$ agree on the covering $\{V\times_UU_i\to V\}$, where both equal $x_{u_i\mathrm{pr}_2}$, so they are equal by separatedness. Conversely gluing on every generated sieve includes gluing for covering families, since a family compatible on the $U_i\times_UU_j$ is the same as a matching family on $\langle u_i\rangle$ via $x_{u_ig}=g^*x_i$. Every $(f,a)\in S$ lies there together with $(f,1)$, since they differ by precomposition with an invertible $(1,a)$. For $E(X)$, compatibility forces $x_{(f,a)}=a\cdot x_{(f,1)}$. The normalized entries form a matching family for $X$ on $S_1$ and hence glue uniquely to $x\in X(U)$; its restrictions along $(f,a)$ give all entries. Conversely, for a base covering sieve $T$, take $S=\{(f,a)\mid f\in T\}$. A base matching family $x_f$ extends uniquely by $x_{(f,a)}=a\cdot x_f$ to a matching family for $N$: along $(g,b)$ its compatibility is $b\cdot g^*(a\cdot x_f)=(b\,g^*a)\cdot x_{fg}$. Gluing on $S$ gives exactly base gluing on $T$. Thus step 1 restricts to the asserted sheaf equivalence. The small-site presentation supplied by the cited node makes this a Grothendieck topos by the definition in [def-weil-pbc-topos].

Finite limits in the action categories are created in underlying sheaves. Explicitly the terminal sheaf has its unique action, a finite product has componentwise action, and the equalizer of equivariant $u,v:X\to Y$ has sections $\{x\mid u(x)=v(x)\}$ with the restricted action. These presheaves are sheaves: compatible tuples glue coordinatewise, and equalizer membership holds after gluing because equality of two sheaf sections can be checked on a cover [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The universal maps into products and equalizers are equivariant by their component equations. Restriction along $\theta$ leaves the terminal object, these products and these equalizers unchanged, and hence preserves finite limits.

Construct the right adjoint on sheaves, not just on individual section sets. For an $L$-object $Y$, define $B(Y)(U)$ to be the set of natural maps of sheaves $F:K|_U\to Y|_U$ on $C/U$ satisfying $F_V(\theta(l)k)=l\cdot F_V(k)$ for every $V\to U$, $l\in L(V)$, $k\in K(V)$. Here slice restriction and its relocalization are those of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Restriction of $F$ defines the presheaf maps. Compatible local maps on a cover of $U$ glue uniquely by the morphism-gluing clause of [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent], applied to $P=K|_U$, $Q=Y|_U$. The glued map is equivariant: over $V\to U$ restrict its required equality to $V\times_U U_i$, where it is the given local equality, and use separatedness of $Y$. Therefore $B(Y)$ is a sheaf. The site and all section sets are small in the fixed universe, so the set of natural maps, a subset of a small product of function sets, remains in that universe [def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: Give $B(Y)$ the $K$-action $(a\cdot F)_V(k)=F_V(k\,a|_V)$. This remains $L$-equivariant because $F_V(\theta(l)k\,a|_V)=l\cdot F_V(k\,a|_V)$. Right translation is natural under base restriction. The identity acts identically, and $(a\cdot(b\cdot F))_V(k)=F_V((k\,a|_V)b|_V)=((ab)\cdot F)_V(k)$. Postcomposing with an $L$-equivariant map $Y\to Y'$ preserves the defining equations, commutes with these translations, and respects identities and compositions. This defines a functor $B:\mathscr E^L\to\mathscr E^K$.

For an $L$-equivariant map $u:q_\theta^{-1}X\to Y$, define $\widehat u_U(x)_V(k)=u_V(k\cdot x|_V)$ for every $V\to U$. It is natural under further restriction, and $\widehat u(x)(\theta(l)k)=l\cdot\widehat u(x)(k)$. Also $\widehat u(a\cdot x)(k)=u((ka)\cdot x)=(a\cdot\widehat u(x))(k)$, so $\widehat u:X\to B(Y)$ is a $K$-map. Conversely a $K$-map $v:X\to B(Y)$ gives $u_U(x)=v_U(x)_U(1)$. Then $u(\theta(l)\cdot x)=(\theta(l)\cdot v(x))(1)=v(x)(\theta(l))=l\cdot v(x)(1)$. Evaluation at $1$ recovers $u$ from $\widehat u$. Starting from $v$, the other composite has value $v(k\cdot x)(1)=(k\cdot v(x))(1)=v(x)(k)$ over every test object, so recovers $v$. These formulas commute with precomposition in $X$ and postcomposition in $Y$. This is the natural Hom bijection $q_\theta^{-1}\dashv B$.

Steps 3 and 6 give the geometric morphism $q_\theta$ by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], taking the structural ring provision only when rings are introduced. For $p_K$, identify actions of the terminal group sheaf $1$ with ordinary sheaves: the unit law forces the sole group element to act identically. Apply the same construction to $K\to1$; its restriction is trivial inflation, its right adjoint is the fixed subsheaf, and step 3 applies. On every section and every map, restriction of a trivial $K$-action is the trivial $L$-action. Thus $q_\theta^{-1}p_K^{-1}=p_L^{-1}$. The identity on these left adjoints gives the canonical geometric isomorphism $p_Kq_\theta\cong p_L$: on right adjoints it is the unique isomorphism representing the same natural Hom functor. Identity restriction and successive restrictions are literally identity and composition because $(\theta\psi)(h)\cdot x=\theta(\psi(h))\cdot x$, with unchanged underlying maps. The associated comparison isomorphisms therefore have their identity and composition coherence.

Apply trivial inflation to the ring operations of $R$. This is exactly the ring sheaf $R_K(U)=R(U)$ with restrictions $R_K(f,a)=f^*$ described in [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation]. Restricting it gives $R_L$ with structural ring map the identity. Similarly $p_K^{-1}R=R_K$ with identity structural map. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], the induced module pullback is $S\otimes_{f^{-1}R}f^{-1}M$. Here $S=f^{-1}R$, so its canonical identification with $f^{-1}M$ sends $r\otimes m$ to $rm$, with inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$; balancing proves the two composites are the identity. The actions on addition and scalar multiplication are just the original ones with trivial inflation or $\theta$-restriction. Thus these identifications give precisely the module functors in the statement, naturally also on linear maps.

Exactness uses the kernel and cokernel assertions, not just the fact that there is a geometric morphism. By [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation], forgetting either action creates the sectionwise kernel and the sheafified sectionwise cokernel; for ordinary module sheaves these are also the descriptions in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Restriction changes neither the underlying module map nor these constructions, and its induced action on their universal maps is the restricted action. Trivial inflation gives trivial actions on both constructions. The canonical comparisons on kernels and cokernels are therefore isomorphisms, with identity underlying maps. Both functors are additive since they leave addition of maps unchanged. Consequently they preserve short exact sequences, proving exactness of both module pullbacks.

Use the actual tensor model [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]: sheafify $U\mapsto M(U)\otimes_{R(U)}N(U)$. On the action site its presheaf restrictions are $x\otimes y\mapsto(a\cdot f^*x)\otimes(a\cdot f^*y)$, hence give the diagonal action. The equivariant sheafification comparison of [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation] identifies its underlying sheaf with the base sheaf tensor. Restricting the action along $\theta$ gives exactly the same presheaf tensor restrictions with $a=\theta(l)$. Trivial inflation likewise gives the trivial action on each tensor. Thus identity on the common presheaf tensors induces the tensor comparisons, whose inverses come from the same identity; the universal property in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] makes them inverse and natural after sheafification. They send $x\otimes y$ to $x\otimes y$. The regular module is $R_K$ (respectively $R_L$), so the unit comparison is the identity on the ring. Compatibility with symmetry, associativity and units follows already on presheaf pure tensors, which generate each sectionwise tensor module; equality descends uniquely through sheafification.

For $\varphi:R\to R'$, put $\varphi_K(U)=\varphi_U$ and $\varphi_L(U)=\varphi_U$. These are ring-sheaf maps with trivial action, since $\varphi$ commutes with base restrictions. The vertical ringed morphisms are the identity geometric morphisms equipped with these structural ring maps, in the direction $(\mathscr E,R')\to(\mathscr E,R)$ and likewise for action topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. In each square involving $p$ or $q$, the inverse-image comparison is the identity from step 7 and both composite structural maps are, on every $U$, exactly $\varphi_U$. Thus the comparison respects the ring maps and gives a commuting square of ringed-topos morphisms. On module pullbacks the same comparison is induced on extension of scalars by $r'\otimes m\mapsto r'\otimes m$, so no further scalar-twisting comparison is implicit.
